paragraphs: (On son of Pelet, Numbers 15:1.) So Seder HaDorot cites from Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 6, beginning of halakhah 5, that he spoke before Rav Yehudah; but the reading Hyman uses is Anan bar Imi. Hyman calls all the names in that passage corrupt and says their readings cannot be established. In the Or Zarua, part 2, locator ספ״ד, the reading is “Chanan bar Imi spoke before Rav Yehudah in the name of Menashe bar Yirmeyah.”

notes.text: The supplied biblical locator is Numbers 15:1, while On son of Pelet belongs to Numbers 16:1; the former is retained in the translation with the difference disclosed. The Or Zarua locator ספ״ד remains literal, not an established “end of chapter 4” or siman 84. That bibliographical question keeps the notice held. Hyman owns the criticism of the Jerusalem Talmud readings.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 108) cites Numbers 16:1, where On son of Pelet appears. The supplied transcription gives 15:1. Seder HaDorot’s notice names On bar Ami. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5, the Hebrew reads אנן כר׳ אימי, while Guggenheimer’s English reads Chanan bar Immi. The consulted Or Zarua, part II, section 84, confirms the quoted reading “Chanan bar Imi spoke before Rav Yehudah in the name of Menashe bar Yirmeyah” in the discussion of hair threads. Hyman’s printed locator ספ״ד is retained in the translation.
